title: The Cotton Club and Small's Paradise, top clubs
summary: The Cotton Club and Small's Paradise were the top clubs; Charlie Johnson produced most of the Small's shows with singers like Mattie Hite.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Broadway didn't have nothing. Everything was in Harlem. The Cotton Club was in Harlem. That was, which you call, the top club in the country -- The Cotton Club.
That was still controlled by all the big boys -- the gangsters in there. You know, it was hard to get in there (inaudible).
Then they had their policies there. Who can get in and --
Oh yeah. They had the policies -- who can get in, you know -- who they would let in.

S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC.

It had all the top names there. Cora Rael Bill Robinson, (inaudible) Dancers. Terrific dancers, Cora Rael you know. (inaudible) leader, you know.
Small's now, you know, Small's Paradise was one of the top clubs too in the country.at that time.
You couldn't hardly get into Small's Paradise no nights.
Charlie Johnson was at that time -- he only had the band there, but Charlie Johnson was producing the shows along with another guy.

He was producing practically ninety percent of the shows. He'd put these shows together -- He would tell the arrangers (inaudible) what I want. "I want to open up this, I want this girl in here, I want this dancer, and I want to (inaudible)," you know.
He would really put on a show. He produced the shows in Atlantic City. He'd bring his singers down.
He had like three girls, you know. Mattie Hite and all these different singers, but they

were all top singers, you know. They'd go out and try to cut each other. They'd volley each other. It was great, you know.

They had a little guy called Jabbo Smith, a little short guy (inaudible). Great shows today -- people talk about one name (inaudible), if they go see the shows today, people will see one name and pay a lot of money for one name.
But back in those days, you had any amount of names in a show. The show was loaded with names, you know.
